title: 1969 AHSME Problem 24
statement: When the natural numbers \(P\) and \(P',\) with \(P\gt P',\) are divided by the natural number \(D,\) the remainders are \(R\) and \(R',\) respectively. When \(PP'\) and \(RR'\) are divided by \(D,\) the remainders are \(r\) and \(r',\) respectively. Then:

solutions.text:
By definition of the remainders, \[ \begin{aligned} P&\equiv R\pmod D,\\ P'&\equiv R'\pmod D. \end{aligned} \] Multiplying gives \(PP'\equiv RR'\pmod D.\) Since each has a unique remainder between \(0\) and \(D-1,\) their remainders must be equal: \(r=r'.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is E.
hints: Write \(P\equiv R\pmod D\) and \(P'\equiv R'\pmod D\)
